John Bicourt led the 5,000 metres field home by a street and Leo Coy stormed down the final stretch to take the 'B' steeplechase. Newcomer Jim Evans showed a flash of great things to come in the 'B' 100 metres.
Bill Kerr showed that Laurie O'Hara is not the only speedy veteran around with his 4:06 timing in the 1500m and Leo Coy improved his steeplechase again, getting closer to 10 minutes.

Our hurdlers and jumpers were devastating and with Leo Coy straight back off his holiday to compete, Lionel Mann gamely vaulting the barriers to fill a gap in our ranks, and John Bicourt offering his services after his trip to Lapland was cancelled, it was a good all-round effort.

Leo Coy clocked a tantalizing 10:02 in the 'chase. After a rare defeat in the short relay our sprinters turned on a marvellous 4 x 400m and showed that a 3:20 time is not beyond the realms of possibility
